\chapter{The Small Ya}
\label{ch:ru-small-ya}
\hlchaptermodality{28}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can write the small ya, the word for I, as Russian writes it inside a sentence.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 28: i can write the small ya, the word for I, as Russian writes it inside a sentence.

\section[ya]{\ru{я} (ya) — the word for I, written small}

\label{lesson:RU-W28-ya-small}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ru{й} and \ru{ю} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ru{я}} (\emph{ya}), \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ru{я}}
\textbf{\ru{я}} — small \emph{ya}.

\textbf{\ru{я}} (\emph{ya}) is also a whole word: \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{}. You wrote the capital \textbf{\ru{Я}} in the letter chapters, but Russian writes \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{} with the \textbf{small} letter: inside a sentence it is never capitalised, unlike English \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{}. So this is the shape you will write most.

\subsection*{Writing: \ru{я}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/RU-W28-ya-small-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ru{я} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: climb the right stem from the baseline to the top
  \item \textbf{2.} without lifting, curve counterclockwise around the upper bowl
  \item \textbf{3.} without lifting, sweep left through the bowl's lower join
  \item \textbf{4.} without lifting, descend the diagonal leg to the lower-left tip — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 0.} The pen never leaves the paper.

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase \ru{я} demonstration, 12:13–12:21, YouTube, 5 February 2013.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ru{я}} and point at \ru{я} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ru{я} three times, saying \emph{ya} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ru{ю}, then \ru{я}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ru{я}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ru{я}? (\textbf{ya}, \emph{ya}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ru{я}}, \emph{ya}, \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
